translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty calls it the 'Celebration Mountain,' but I hold that it is no cause for celebration.

sentences.zh: 宜側身脩德以答天譴，不然，恐災禍至。

translations.literal: You should turn inward and cultivate virtue to answer Heaven's reproof; otherwise, I fear disaster and calamity will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: You should turn inward and cultivate virtue to answer Heaven's reproof; otherwise, I fear disaster will follow.

sentences.zh: 」后怒，流于嶺南。

translations.literal: " The Empress was enraged and had him exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: " The Empress was enraged and had him exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 永昌中，華州赤水南岸大山，晝日忽風昏，有聲隱隱如雷，頃之漸移東數百步，擁赤水，壓張村民三十餘家，山高二百餘丈，水深三十丈，坡上草木宛然。

translations.literal: During the Yongchang era, on the south bank of the Chishui in Huazhou, a great mountain—in broad daylight wind suddenly darkened the sky, and there was a faint sound like thunder; shortly it gradually shifted east several hundred paces, pressing against the Chishui and crushing more than thirty households of Zhang village; the mountain was more than two hundred zhang high, the water thirty zhang deep, and the grasses and trees on the slope remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchang era (689), on the south bank of the Chishui in Huazhou, a great mountain—in broad daylight the wind suddenly darkened the sky and a faint rumbling like thunder was heard; shortly the mountain shifted east several hundred paces, pressing against the Chishui and crushing more than thirty households of Zhang village; the mountain stood more than two hundred zhang high, the water thirty zhang deep, and the grasses and trees on the slope remained intact as before.

sentences.zh: 金縢曰：「山徙者人君不用道，祿去公室，賞罰不由君，佞人執政，政在女主，不出五年，有走王。

translations.literal: The Metal Casket says: "When mountains shift, the ruler does not follow the Way; emoluments leave the public house; rewards and punishments are not decided by the ruler; flatterers hold power; government lies with a female ruler; within five years there will be a fleeing king."
translations.idiomatic: The Metal Casket says: "When mountains shift, the ruler has abandoned the Way; emoluments leave the royal house; rewards and punishments no longer rest with the ruler; flatterers hold power; government lies with a woman; within five years there will be a king who flees."

sentences.zh: 開元十七年四月乙亥，大風震電，藍田山摧裂百餘步，畿內山也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on the yihai day, of the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan, a great wind with thunder and lightning; Lantian Mountain collapsed and split for more than a hundred paces—it was a mountain within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan (729), on the yihai day, a great wind with thunder and lightning struck; Lantian Mountain collapsed and split open for more than a hundred paces—it was a mountain within the capital region.

sentences.zh: 國主山川，山摧川竭，亡之證也。

translations.literal: The ruler of a state presides over mountains and rivers; when mountains collapse and rivers are exhausted, these are proofs of destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of a state presides over its mountains and rivers; when mountains collapse and rivers run dry, these are signs of a state's ruin.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「人君德消政易則然。

translations.literal: The omen reading says: "When the ruler's virtue fades and government changes, then this occurs."
translations.idiomatic: The omen reading says: "When the ruler's virtue fades and government turns corrupt, then this occurs."

sentences.zh: 大曆九年十一月戊戌，同州夏陽有山徙于河上，聲如雷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the wuxu day, of the ninth year of Dali, in Xiayang, Tongzhou, a mountain moved onto the river; the sound was like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the ninth year of Dali (774), on the wuxu day, a mountain in Xiayang, Tongzhou, shifted onto the river with a sound like thunder.

sentences.zh: 十三年，郴州黃芩山摧，壓死者數百人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Huangqin Mountain in Chenzhou collapsed; several hundred people were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (778), Huangqin Mountain in Chenzhou collapsed, crushing several hundred people to death.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，霍山裂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, Huo Mountain split.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong (781), Huo Mountain split open.

sentences.zh: 元和八年五月丁丑，大隗山摧。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the dingchou day, of the eighth year of Yuanhe, Great Wei Mountain collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Yuanhe (813), on the dingchou day, Great Wei Mountain collapsed.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月丁未，苑中土山摧，壓死二十人。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on the dingwei day, of the fifteenth year, an earthen mountain in the park collapsed; twenty people were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifteenth year (820), on the dingwei day, an earthen hill in the imperial park collapsed, crushing twenty people to death.

sentences.zh: 光啟三年四月，維州山崩，累日不止，塵坌亙天，壅江水逆流。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Guangqi, a mountain in Weizhou collapsed; for days it did not cease; dust filled the sky; it blocked the river and the water flowed backward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Guangqi (887), a mountain in Weizhou collapsed and went on for days without cease; dust filled the sky, dammed the river, and forced the water to flow backward.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「國破。

translations.literal: The omen reading says: "The state is broken.
translations.idiomatic: The omen reading says: "The state will be broken.

sentences.zh: 山鳴。

translations.literal: Mountains rumbling.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains rumbling.

sentences.zh: 武德二年三月，太行山聖人崖有聲。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Wude, at Sage Cliff on the Taihang Mountains, there was a sound.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Wude (619), Sage Cliff in the Taihang Mountains gave forth a sound.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有寇至。

translations.literal: The omen reading says: "Invaders will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The omen reading says: "Invaders will arrive.

sentences.zh: 開元二十八年六月，吐蕃圍安戎城，斷水路，城東山鳴石坼，湧泉二。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year of Kaiyuan, the Tibetans besieged Anrong Fortress and cut off the water route; east of the city a mountain rumbled, stones split, and two springs burst forth.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year of Kaiyuan (740), the Tibetans besieged Anrong Fortress and cut off its water supply; east of the city a mountain rumbled, stones split open, and two springs gushed forth.

sentences.zh: 土為變怪。

translations.literal: Earth manifesting strange transformations.
translations.idiomatic: Earth manifesting strange transformations.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年九月，淮南地生毛，或白或蒼，長者尺餘，遍居人牀下，揚州尤甚，大如馬鬣，焚之臭如燎毛。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Chuigong, hair grew from the ground in Huainan, white or gray-green; the longest were more than a chi; it spread beneath people's beds everywhere; Yangzhou was especially severe; some were as large as a horse's mane; when burned, the smell was like singeing hair.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Chuigong (685), hair sprouted from the ground in Huainan, white or gray-green, some more than a foot long; it spread beneath people's beds everywhere, Yangzhou worst of all, some tufts as large as a horse's mane; when burned, they smelled of singed hair.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「兵起，民不安。

translations.literal: The omen reading says: "Armies will arise; the people will be unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The omen reading says: "War will arise; the people will be unsettled.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，東都天宮寺泥像皆流汗霢霂。

translations.literal: During the Changshou era, the clay statues at Tiangong Temple in the Eastern Capital all sweated in a fine drizzle.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changshou era (692–694), the clay statues at Tiangong Temple in the Eastern Capital all sweated in a fine, steady drizzle.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載六月，虢州閺鄉黃河中女媧墓因大雨晦冥，失其所在，至乾元二年六月乙未夜，瀕河人聞有風雷聲，曉見其墓踊出，下有巨石，上有雙柳，各長丈餘，時號風陵堆。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eleventh year of Tianbao, the tomb of Nüwa in the Yellow River at Yinyi, Guozhou, was lost in heavy rain and murky darkness; until the night of the sixth month, on the yiwei day, of the second year of Qianyuan, people along the river heard wind and thunder; at dawn they saw the tomb burst forth; beneath it was a great stone, and upon it were twin willows, each more than a zhang long; at the time it was called Fengling Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eleventh year of Tianbao (752), the tomb of Nüwa in the Yellow River at Yinyi in Guozhou was lost to sight in heavy rain and murky darkness; then on the night of the sixth month of the second year of Qianyuan (759), the yiwei day, people along the river heard wind and thunder, and at dawn saw the tomb thrust up from the water; beneath it lay a great stone, and upon it stood twin willows, each more than a zhang tall; at the time it was called Fengling Mound.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「塚墓自移，天下破。

translations.literal: The omen reading says: "When tombs and graves shift of themselves, the realm is broken.
translations.idiomatic: The omen reading says: "When tombs and graves shift of themselves, the realm will be broken.

sentences.zh: 」十三載，汝州葉縣南有土塊鬬，中有血出，數日不止。

translations.literal: " In the thirteenth year, south of Ye County in Ruzhou, clods of earth fought one another; blood issued from within them, and for several days it did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: " In the thirteenth year (754), south of Ye County in Ruzhou, clods of earth fought one another; blood welled from within them and flowed for several days without cease.

sentences.zh: 大曆六年四月戊寅，藍田西原地陷。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on the wuyin day, of the sixth year of Dali, the ground subsided on the western plain of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year of Dali (771), on the wuyin day, the ground subsided on the western plain of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 建中初，魏州魏縣西四十里，地數畝忽長崇數尺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, forty li west of Wei County in Weizhou, several mu of ground suddenly rose several chi high.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era (circa 780), forty li west of Wei County in Weizhou, several mu of ground suddenly swelled several chi high.

sentences.zh: 四年四月甲子，京師地生毛，或黃或白，有長尺餘者。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on the jiazi day, of the fourth year, hair grew from the ground in the capital, yellow or white; some were more than a chi long.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year (783), on the jiazi day, hair sprouted from the ground in the capital, yellow or white, some more than a foot long.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年四月，淮南及河南地生毛。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan, hair grew from the ground in Huainan and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan (788), hair sprouted from the ground in Huainan and Henan.

sentences.zh: 元和十二年四月，吳元濟郾城守將鄧懷金以城降，城自壞五十餘步。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year of Yuanhe, Deng Huaijin, the defending general of Yancheng under Wu Yuanji, surrendered the city; the city wall collapsed of its own accord for more than fifty paces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twelfth year of Yuanhe (817), Deng Huaijin, the defending general of Yancheng under Wu Yuanji, surrendered the city, whereupon the city wall collapsed of its own for more than fifty paces.

sentences.zh: 大和六年二月，蘇州地震，生白毛。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Dahe, Suzhou had an earthquake and white hair sprouted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year of Dahe (832), Suzhou was shaken by an earthquake, and white hair sprouted from the ground.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，新都大道觀泥人生須數寸，拔之復生。

translations.literal: During the Changqing era, at Dadao Abbey in Xindu the clay figures grew beards several cun long; when plucked out they grew again.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing era (821–824), the clay figures at Dadao Abbey in Xindu grew beards several inches long; plucked out, they grew back again.

sentences.zh: 咸通五年十月，貞陵隧道摧陷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year of Xiantong, the tunnel of Zhenling collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifth year of Xiantong (864), the tunnel of Emperor Yizong's Zhenling tomb collapsed.

sentences.zh: 神策軍有浮屠像，懿宗嘗跪禮之，像沒地四尺。

translations.literal: The Shence Army had a Buddhist statue; Emperor Yizong once knelt and paid it reverence, and the statue sank four chi into the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The Shence Army possessed a Buddhist statue; Emperor Yizong once knelt and paid it reverence, and the statue sank four feet into the ground.

sentences.zh: 五行傳曰：「好攻戰，輕百姓，飾城郭，侵邊境，則金不從革。

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Five Elements says: "If one loves warfare, treats the common people lightly, adorns walls and ramparts, and encroaches on borderlands, then metal does not obey transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Five Elements states: "When rulers love warfare, treat the common people lightly, adorn walls and ramparts, and encroach on the borderlands, then metal does not obey transformation.

sentences.zh: 」謂金失其性而為變怪也。

translations.literal: " This means that when metal loses its proper nature it becomes strange transformations.
translations.idiomatic: This refers to metal losing its proper character and manifesting as strange transformations.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「言之不從，是謂不乂。

translations.literal: It also says: "If words are not followed, this is called lack of governance.
translations.idiomatic: It further says: "When words are not heeded, this is called lack of good governance.

sentences.zh: 厥咎僭，厥罰常暘，厥極憂。

translations.literal: Its blame is presumption, its penalty is constant drought, its extreme is sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The blame lies in presumption, the penalty in constant drought, and the extreme manifestation in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 時則有詩妖、訛言，時則有毛蟲之孽，時則有太禍，時則有口舌之痾，時則有白眚白祥，惟木沴金。

translations.literal: At times there are poetic omens and false reports; at times calamities of hairy insects; at times great disasters; at times ailments of the mouth and tongue; at times white omens and white auspices; only wood injures metal.
translations.idiomatic: Then come poetic omens and slanderous rumors; calamities of hairy insects; great disasters; diseases of speech; white omens and white auspices; and wood alone harming metal.

sentences.zh: 金不從革。

translations.literal: Metal not obeying transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Metal failing to obey transformation.

sentences.zh: 堯君素為隋守蒲州，兵器夜皆有光如火。

translations.literal: Yao Junsu was defending Puzhou for Sui; at night all weapons had light like fire.
translations.idiomatic: While Yao Junsu held Puzhou for the Sui, at night all the weapons gleamed like fire.

sentences.zh: 火鑠金，金所畏也，敗亡之象。

translations.literal: Fire melts metal; it is what metal fears; an image of defeat and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Fire melts metal—metal's natural dread—and this was an omen of defeat and ruin.

sentences.zh: 劉武周據幷州，兵勢甚盛，城上矟刃夜每有火光。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou held Bingzhou; his military strength was very great; on the city walls the spear blades each night had fire-light.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou held Bingzhou at the height of his power; each night the spear blades on the city walls gleamed with firelight.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十七年八月，涼州昌松縣鴻池谷有石五，青質白文成字曰：「高皇海出多子李元王八十年太平天子李世民千年太子李治書燕山人士樂太國主尚汪譂奬文仁邁千古大王五王六王七王十風毛才子七佛八菩薩及上果佛田天子文武貞觀昌大聖延四方上不治示孝仙戈八為善。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, at Hongchi Valley in Changsong County, Liangzhou, there were five stones; green in substance with white writing forming characters that read: 「高皇海出多子李元王八十年太平天子李世民千年太子李治書燕山人士樂太國主尚汪譂奬文仁邁千古大王五王六王七王十風毛才子七佛八菩薩及上果佛田天子文武貞觀昌大聖延四方上不治示孝仙戈八為善。
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year of Zhenguan (643), at Hongchi Valley in Changsong County, Liangzhou, five green stones appeared bearing white inscriptions prophesying the reign of Emperor Gaozu Li Yuan, the eighty-year rule of Taiping Son of Heaven Li Shimin (Emperor Taizong), the thousand-year succession of Crown Prince Li Zhi, titles for princes and talented men, praise for the Wen-Wu Son of Heaven, and the flourishing Zhenguan era of great sagehood extending in all directions.

sentences.zh: 」太宗遣使祭之曰：「天有成命，表瑞貞石，文字昭然，曆數惟永，既旌高廟之業，又錫眇身之祚。

translations.literal: " Emperor Taizong sent an envoy to sacrifice to them, saying: 「Heaven holds a completed mandate; the stone omen displays auspiciousness; the written characters are manifest; the succession alone is eternal; it both commends the achievement of the High Temple and bestows the throne upon this insignificant person.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Taizong sent an envoy to make sacrifice, saying: 「Heaven has fulfilled its mandate; the auspicious stone displays its portent; the characters shine clearly; the succession is everlasting; it honors the ancestral temple's achievement and grants this unworthy person the throne.

sentences.zh: 迨于皇太子治，亦降貞符，具紀姓氏。

translations.literal: Reaching to the Crown Prince Zhi, it also sends down tokens of faithfulness, fully recording surnames and clans.
translations.idiomatic: It extends even to Crown Prince Zhi, granting tokens of legitimacy and recording the imperial surname in full.

sentences.zh: 甫惟寡薄，彌增寅懼。

translations.literal: I am only meager and slight; I increase my reverence and fear yet more.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy and slight, and this only deepens my reverence and alarm.

sentences.zh: 」昔魏以土德代漢，涼州石有文。

translations.literal: " In former times Wei succeeded Han by the virtue of earth, and stones in Liangzhou bore writing.
translations.idiomatic: " In former times Wei replaced Han under the virtue of earth, and stones in Liangzhou bore inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 石，金類，以五勝推之，故時人謂為魏氏之妖，而晉室之瑞。

translations.literal: Stone is a kind of metal; by inference from the five conquests, people of the time called it an evil omen for Wei and an auspice for Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Stone belongs to the metal phase; by the logic of mutual conquest among the five phases, people at the time took it as an ill omen for Wei and an auspice for Jin.

sentences.zh: 唐亦土德王，石有文，事頗相類。

translations.literal: Tang also reigned by the virtue of earth; stones bore writing; the matter is quite similar.
translations.idiomatic: Tang also ruled under the virtue of earth, and inscribed stones appeared—a case much the same.

sentences.zh: 然其文初不可曉，而後人因推已事以驗之。

translations.literal: Yet at first the writing could not be understood, and later people inferred events already past to verify it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at first the inscription could not be deciphered; later people retrofitted past events to confirm it.

sentences.zh: 蓋武氏革命，自以為金德王，其「佛菩薩」者，慈氏金輪之號也；

translations.literal: Presumably the Wu clan's revolution claimed to reign by the virtue of metal; its 「Buddhas and Bodhisattvas」 was the title of the Maitreya Golden Wheel;
translations.idiomatic: Presumably the Wu clan's revolution, claiming to reign under the virtue of metal, took its 「Buddhas and Bodhisattvas」 as the title of the Maitreya Golden Wheel;

sentences.zh: 「樂太國主」則鎮國太平公主、安樂公主，皆以女亂國；

translations.literal: 「Lord of Joy in the Great State」 refers to the Princess Zhenguo Taiping and Princess Anle—both brought disorder to the state through women;
translations.idiomatic: 「Lord of Joy in the Great State」 referred to Princess Zhenguo Taiping and Princess Anle—both of whom brought the state to disorder through women;

sentences.zh: 其「五王六王七王」者，唐世十八之數。

translations.literal: Its 「Five Kings, Six Kings, and Seven Kings」 refers to the number eighteen in the Tang age.
translations.idiomatic: Its 「Five Kings, Six Kings, and Seven Kings」 pointed to the number eighteen among Tang emperors.

sentences.zh: 垂拱三年七月，魏州地出鐵如船數十丈。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Chuigong, from the ground in Weizhou iron emerged like a ship dozens of zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year of Chuigong (687), iron emerged from the ground in Weizhou in a mass like a ship dozens of feet long.

sentences.zh: 廣州雨金。

translations.literal: In Guangzhou, gold rained.
translations.idiomatic: Gold rained in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 金位正秋，為刑、為兵。

translations.literal: Metal's position is mid-autumn; it stands for punishment and for war.
translations.idiomatic: Metal corresponds to mid-autumn; it signifies punishment and warfare.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「人君多殺無辜，一年兵災于朝。

translations.literal: The omen reading says: "The ruler kills many innocent people; within a year military disaster at court.
translations.idiomatic: The omen reading says: "When the ruler kills many innocent people, within a year military disaster will strike at court.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年十二月乙巳，龍池聖德頌石自鳴，其音清遠如鐘磬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the yisi day, of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, the stone of the Ode to Sagely Virtue of Dragon Pool rang of itself; its sound was clear and distant like bells and chimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan (735), on the yisi day, the stone bearing the Ode to Sagely Virtue of Dragon Pool rang of itself, its tone clear and far-reaching like bells and chimes.

sentences.zh: 石與金同類。

translations.literal: Stone belongs to the same category as metal.
translations.idiomatic: Stone belongs to the same category as metal.

sentences.zh: 春秋傳「怨讟動于民，則有非言之物言。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary: 「When resentment and slander stir among the people, then things that do not speak will speak.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says: 「When resentment and slander stir among the people, then things that do not speak will speak.

sentences.zh: 」石鳴，近石言也。

translations.literal: " Stones ringing—this approximates stones speaking.
translations.idiomatic: " Stones ringing—this approximates stones speaking.

sentences.zh: 天寶十載六月乙亥，大同殿前鐘自鳴。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the yihai day, of the tenth year of Tianbao, the bell before the Datong Hall rang of itself.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the tenth year of Tianbao (751), on the yihai day, the bell before the Datong Hall rang of itself.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「庶雄為亂。

translations.literal: The omen reading says: "Lesser strongmen will rise in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The omen reading says: "Lesser strongmen will rise in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，昭陵石馬汗出。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide, the stone horses at Zhaoling sweated.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide (757), the stone horses at Emperor Taizong's Zhaoling Mausoleum sweated.

sentences.zh: 昔周武帝之克晉州也，齊有石像，汗流濕地，此其類也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Emperor Wu of Zhou captured Jizhou, Qi had a stone image whose sweat soaked the ground—this is of that kind.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou captured Jizhou, a stone image in Qi sweated until the ground was soaked—this was of the same kind.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年七月乙亥晝，渾天儀有液如汗下流。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on the yihai day, of the second year of Qianyuan, at midday the armillary sphere had liquid like sweat flowing down.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Qianyuan (759), on the yihai day, at midday the armillary sphere exuded liquid like sweat flowing downward.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，楚州獻寶玉十三：曰「玄黃天符」，形如笏，長八寸，有孔，云辟兵疫；

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan, Chuzhou presented thirteen precious jades: one called 「Black and Yellow Heavenly Talisman」, shaped like a tablet, eight cun long, with a hole, said to ward off arms and pestilence;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shangyuan (761), Chuzhou presented thirteen precious jades: one called 「Black and Yellow Heavenly Talisman」, shaped like an official tablet, eight inches long, with a hole, said to ward off warfare and pestilence;

sentences.zh: 曰「玉雞毛」，白玉也；

translations.literal: one called 「Jade Cock Feather」, white jade;
translations.idiomatic: one called 「Jade Cock Feather」, of white jade;

sentences.zh: 曰「穀璧」，亦白玉也，粟粒自然，無雕鐫迹；

translations.literal: one called 「Grain Disk」, also white jade, with millet grains natural, without carved or incised marks;
translations.idiomatic: one called 「Grain Disk」, also of white jade, with millet grains formed naturally and no trace of carving or incising;

sentences.zh: 曰「西王母白環」二；

translations.literal: two called 「White Ring of the Queen Mother of the West」;
translations.idiomatic: two called 「White Ring of the Queen Mother of the West」;

sentences.zh: 曰「如意寶珠」，大如雞卵；

translations.literal: one called 「Wishing-fulfillment Precious Pearl」, as large as a chicken's egg;
translations.idiomatic: one called 「Wishing-fulfillment Precious Pearl」, as large as a chicken's egg;

sentences.zh: 曰「紅靺鞨」，大如巨粟；

translations.literal: one called 「Red Mohe」, as large as a large millet grain;
translations.idiomatic: one called 「Red Mohe」, as large as a large grain of millet;

sentences.zh: 曰「琅玕珠」二，形如玉環，四分缺一；

translations.literal: two called 「Langgan Pearls」, shaped like jade rings, one quarter missing;
translations.idiomatic: two called 「Langgan Pearls」, shaped like jade rings with one quarter missing;

sentences.zh: 曰「玉印」，大如半手，理如鹿，陷入印中；

translations.literal: one called 「Jade Seal」, half the size of a hand, with deer-like grain sunk into the seal;
translations.idiomatic: one called 「Jade Seal」, half the size of a hand, with a deer-like grain pattern sunk into the seal;

sentences.zh: 曰「皇后採桑鉤」如箸屈其末；

translations.literal: one called 「Queen's Silkworm-gathering Hook」, like chopsticks with the tip bent;
translations.idiomatic: one called 「Queen's Silkworm-gathering Hook」, like chopsticks with the tip bent inward;

sentences.zh: 曰「雷公石斧」無孔；

translations.literal: one called 「Lord of Thunder's Stone Axe」, without a hole;
translations.idiomatic: one called 「Lord of Thunder's Stone Axe」, without a hole;

sentences.zh: 其一闕。

translations.literal: One was missing.
translations.idiomatic: One piece was missing.

sentences.zh: 凡十三。

translations.literal: In all, thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: In all, thirteen.

sentences.zh: 寘之日中，白氣連天。

translations.literal: When placed in the sun at midday, white vapor reached the sky.
translations.idiomatic: When they were placed in the sun at midday, white vapor rose to the sky.

sentences.zh: 元和中，文水武士彠碑失其龜頭。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era, the tortoise head of Wu Shiyi's stele in Wenshui was lost.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era (806–820), the tortoise head of Wu Shiyi's stele in Wenshui was lost.

sentences.zh: 翰林院有鈴，夜中文書入，則引之以代傳呼，長慶中，河北用兵，夜輒自鳴，與軍中息耗相應，聲急則軍事急，聲緩則軍事緩。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academy had a bell; at night when documents entered, it was rung to replace calling out. During Changqing, when Hebei was at war, at night it rang of itself, corresponding to military news—when the sound was urgent, military affairs were urgent; when slow, affairs were slow.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin Academy had a bell that was rung at night when documents arrived, replacing shouted announcements. During the Changqing era (821–824), while Hebei was at war, it rang of itself at night in correspondence with military news—when the sound was urgent, military affairs were urgent; when slow, affairs were slow.

sentences.zh: 資州有石方丈，走行數畝。

translations.literal: In Zizhou there was a square stone one zhang across that walked, traversing several mu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zizhou there was a square stone one zhang across that moved on its own, traveling several mu.

sentences.zh: 大和三年，南蠻圍成都，毀玉晨殿為礧，有吼聲三，乃止。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dahe, southern barbarians besieged Chengdu and destroyed the Yuchen Hall for siege engines; there were three roars, then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dahe (829), southern tribes besieged Chengdu and demolished the Yuchen Hall for catapult stones; there were three roars, then it stopped.

sentences.zh: 四年五月己卯，通化南北二門鎖不可開，鑰入，如有持之者。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the jimao day, of the fourth year, the locks on the north and south gates of Tonghua could not be opened; when the key was inserted, it was as if someone held it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year (830), on the jimao day, the locks on the north and south gates of Tonghua could not be opened; when the key was inserted, it was as if someone held it fast.

sentences.zh: 破其管，門乃啟。

translations.literal: When the lock cylinder was broken, the gate then opened.
translations.idiomatic: When the lock cylinder was broken, the gate then opened.

sentences.zh: 又浙西觀察使王璠治潤州城隍，中得方石，有刻文曰：「山有石，石有玉，玉有瑕，瑕即休。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhexi Observation Commissioner Wang Fan repaired the wall and moat of Runzhou and found a square stone within, with inscribed text reading: 「In mountains there is stone; in stone there is jade; in jade there is a flaw—when the flaw appears, stop.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zhexi Observation Commissioner Wang Fan repaired the wall and moat of Runzhou and found a square stone within, with an inscription reading: 「In mountains there is stone; in stone there is jade; in jade there is a flaw—when the flaw appears, stop.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年，華岳廟玄宗御製碑隱隱然有聲，聞數里間，浹旬乃止。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangming, at Mount Hua's temple the stele inscribed by Emperor Xuanzong faintly made a sound audible for several li; after ten days it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangming (880), at the Mount Hua temple the stele inscribed by Emperor Xuanzong faintly gave forth a sound audible for several li; after ten days it stopped.

sentences.zh: 近石言也。

translations.literal: This approximates stones speaking.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates stones speaking.

sentences.zh: 光化三年冬，武德殿前鐘聲忽嘶嗄；

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Guanghua, the bell before Wude Hall suddenly turned hoarse and raspy;
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Guanghua (900), the bell before Wude Hall suddenly turned hoarse and raspy;

sentences.zh: 天復元年九月，聲又變小。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Tianfu, the sound again grew smaller.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Tianfu (901), the sound again grew smaller.

sentences.zh: 常暘。

translations.literal: Constant drought.
translations.idiomatic: Persistent drought.

sentences.zh: 武德三年夏，旱，至于八月乃雨。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year of Wude, drought; until the eighth month it then rained.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year of Wude (620), drought persisted until rain finally came in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 四年，自春不雨，至于七月。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, from spring there was no rain until the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (621), no rain fell from spring until the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 雨，少陰之氣，其氣毀則不雨。

translations.literal: Rain is the qi of lesser yin; when its qi is destroyed, there is no rain.
translations.idiomatic: Rain belongs to the qi of lesser yin; when that qi is damaged, rain fails.

sentences.zh: 少陰者，金也，金為刑、為兵，刑不辜，兵不戢，則金氣毀，故常為旱。

translations.literal: Lesser yin is metal; metal stands for punishment and for war; when punishment falls on the innocent and war is not restrained, then the qi of metal is destroyed, and so drought is constant.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser yin is metal; metal signifies punishment and warfare; when the innocent are punished and armies are not restrained, the qi of metal is damaged, and drought commonly follows.

sentences.zh: 火為盛陽，陽氣彊悍，故聖人制禮以節之。

translations.literal: Fire is flourishing yang; yang qi is fierce and overbearing; therefore the sages established ritual to restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: Fire is flourishing yang; yang qi is fierce and overbearing; therefore the sages established ritual to restrain it.

sentences.zh: 禮失則僭而驕炕，以導盛陽，火勝則金衰，故亦旱。

translations.literal: When ritual is lost there is presumption, pride, and arrogance, guiding flourishing yang; when fire prevails, metal declines, and so there is also drought.
translations.idiomatic: When ritual fails, presumption, pride, and arrogance arise, feeding flourishing yang; when fire overcomes metal, drought follows as well.

sentences.zh: 於五行，土實制水，土功興則水氣壅閼，又常為旱。

translations.literal: Among the five phases, earth truly restrains water; when earthworks rise, the qi of water is blocked and obstructed, and drought again is constant.
translations.idiomatic: Among the five phases, earth truly restrains water; when earthworks are undertaken on a large scale, the qi of water is obstructed, and drought commonly results.

sentences.zh: 天官有東井，主水事，天漢、天江，亦水祥也。

translations.literal: In the celestial offices there is the Eastern Well, governing water affairs; the Celestial River and Heavenly River are also water omens.
translations.idiomatic: In the celestial offices there is the Eastern Well, governing water affairs; the Celestial River and Heavenly River are also water omens.

sentences.zh: 水與火仇，而受制于土，土火謫見，若日蝕過分而未至，與七曜循中道之南，皆旱祥也。

translations.literal: Water is at odds with fire yet is restrained by earth; when earth and fire appear as censures, as when an eclipse passes the allotted degree but has not yet arrived, and when the seven luminaries follow the south of the middle way—all are drought omens.
translations.idiomatic: Water is hostile to fire yet subject to earth's restraint; when earth and fire appear as censures—as when an eclipse passes the allotted degree without fully arriving, or when the seven luminaries travel south of the middle path—all are drought omens.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，關內、河東旱。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year, drought in Guannei and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year of Wude (624), drought struck Guannei and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年夏，山東大旱。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Zhenguan, great drought in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Zhenguan (627), Shandong suffered severe drought.

sentences.zh: 二年春，旱。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year (628), drought.

sentences.zh: 三年春、夏，旱。

translations.literal: In the spring and summer of the third year, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring and summer of the third year (629), drought.

sentences.zh: 四年春，旱。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year (630), drought.

sentences.zh: 自太上皇傳位至此，而比年水旱。

translations.literal: From the abdication of the Taishang Huang to this point, year after year there were floods and droughts.
translations.idiomatic: From the Taishang Huang's abdication to this point, flood and drought struck year after year.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，劍南、關東州二十四，旱。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year, twenty-four prefectures in Jiannan and Guandong, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the ninth year (635), twenty-four prefectures in Jiannan and Guandong suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 十二年，吳、楚、巴、蜀州二十六，旱；

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, twenty-six prefectures in Wu, Chu, Ba, and Shu, drought;

sentences.zh: 太常丞李嗣真曰：「側者，不正；

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Sizhen said: "Ce means not upright;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Sizhen said: "Ce means not upright;

sentences.zh: 橈者，不安。

translations.literal: rao means unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: rao means unsettled.

translations.idiomatic: Since the Sui, the Music Bureau has had a Tangtang tune; to speak of tangtang twice is an image of Tang receiving the mandate anew.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年七月，東都大雨，人多殍殕。

translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongchun (682), heavy rain struck the Eastern Capital, and many people died of exposure and starvation.

sentences.zh: 先是童謠曰：「新禾不入箱，新麥不入場，迨及八九月，狗吠空垣牆。

translations.idiomatic: Earlier a children's rhyme had run: "New rice never reaches the bin, new wheat never reaches the threshing floor; by the eighth and ninth months, dogs bark at empty courtyard walls.

sentences.zh: 高宗自調露中欲封嵩山，屬突厥叛而止；

translations.literal: From the Diaolu era onward Emperor Gaozong wished to perform the feng and shan rites at Mount Song, but stopped when the Turks rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: From the Diaolu era onward Emperor Gaozong wished to perform the feng and shan rites at Mount Song, but stopped when the Turks rebelled;

sentences.zh: 後又欲封，以吐蕃入寇遂停。

translations.literal: Later he again wished to perform the rites, but halted when Tibet invaded.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again wished to perform the rites, but halted when Tibet invaded.

sentences.zh: 時童謠曰：「嵩山凡幾層，不畏登不得，但恐不得登，三度徵兵馬，傍道朾騰騰。

translations.literal: At the time a children's rhyme said: "嵩山凡幾層, 不畏登不得, 但恐不得登, 三度徵兵馬, 傍道朾騰騰.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a children's rhyme ran: "Mount Song has how many tiers? Do not fear that one cannot climb; only fear that one will not be allowed to climb. Three times troops are levied, and along the road they stamp and thunder.

sentences.zh: 永徽末，里歌有桑條韋也、女時韋也樂。

translations.literal: At the end of Yonghui, among neighborhood songs there were "Sangtiao Wei ye" and "Nüshi Wei ye le."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yonghui era (655), neighborhood songs included "Sangtiao Wei ye" and "Nüshi Wei ye le."

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，時人飲酒令曰：「子母相去離，連臺拗倒。

translations.literal: During Longshuo, people's drinking-game verses said: "子母相去離, 連臺拗倒.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longshuo era (661–663), drinking-game verses ran: "Mother and child part and separate; linked trays topple together.

sentences.zh: 」俗謂盃盤為子母，又名盤為臺。

translations.literal: 」 The common people call cups and plates "mother and child," and also call a plate a "platform."
translations.idiomatic: " The common people called cups and plates "mother and child," and also called a plate a "platform."

sentences.zh: 又里歌有突厥鹽。

translations.literal: Again, among neighborhood songs there was "Tujue yan."
translations.idiomatic: Neighborhood songs also included "Tujue yan" (Turkic salt).

sentences.zh: 永淳後，民歌曰：「楊柳楊柳漫頭駝。

translations.literal: After Yongchun, the people sang: "楊柳楊柳漫頭駝.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongchun era, the people sang: "Willow, willow, camels cover the head.

sentences.zh: 垂拱後，東都有契苾兒歌，皆淫豔之詞。

translations.literal: After Chuigong, in the Eastern Capital there were Qibi'er songs, all lascivious and sensual in wording.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chuigong era (685 onward), the Eastern Capital had Qibi'er songs, all lascivious in wording.

sentences.zh: 契苾，張易之小字也。

translations.literal: Qibi was the childhood name of Zhang Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi was the childhood name of Zhang Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 如意初，里歌曰：「黃麞黃麞草裏藏，彎弓射爾傷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ruyi, a neighborhood song said: "黃麞黃麞草裏藏, 彎弓射爾傷.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Ruyi era (692), a neighborhood song ran: "Yellow river-deer, yellow river-deer, hiding in the grass—bending the bow, I shoot and wound you.

sentences.zh: 」其後，壬孝傑敗於黃麞谷。

translations.literal: 」 Afterward, Wang Xiaojie was defeated at Huangzhi Valley.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Wang Xiaojie was defeated at Huangzhi Valley.

sentences.zh: 神龍以後，民謠曰：「山南烏鵲窠，山北金駱駝，鐮柯不鑿孔，斧子不施柯。

translations.literal: After Shenlong, a folk rhyme said: "山南烏鵲窠, 山北金駱駝, 鐮柯不鑿孔, 斧子不施柯.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shenlong era (705 onward), a folk rhyme ran: "South of the mountains, magpie nests; north of the mountains, golden camels. The sickle handle needs no bored hole; the axe needs no fitted helve.

sentences.zh: 」山南，唐也，烏鵲窠者，人居寡也；

translations.literal: 」 South of the mountains is Tang; magpie nests mean few people dwelling;
translations.idiomatic: " "South of the mountains" is Tang; "magpie nests" means few people dwelling;

sentences.zh: 山北，胡也，金駱駝者，虜獲而重載也。

translations.literal: North of the mountains is the Hu; golden camels mean barbarians captured and heavily laden.
translations.idiomatic: "North of the mountains" is the barbarians; "golden camels" means captives taken and heavily laden with booty.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主於洛州造安樂寺，童謠曰：「可憐安樂寺，了了樹頭懸。

translations.literal: Princess Anle built Anle Temple in Luozhou; a children's rhyme said: "可憐安樂寺, 了了樹頭懸.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle built Anle Temple in Luozhou; a children's rhyme ran: "Pitiable Anle Temple—clearly hung from the treetops.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，民謠曰：「黃牸犢子挽紖斷，兩足踏地鞵𪎱斷，城南黃牸犢子韋。

translations.literal: During Jinglong, a folk rhyme said: "黃牸犢子挽紖斷, 兩足踏地鞵𪎱斷, 城南黃牸犢子韋.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era (707–710), a folk rhyme ran: "The yellow heifer calf breaks the harness rope; both feet on the ground, the shoe straps snap—south of the city, the yellow heifer calf is Wei.

sentences.zh: 」又有阿緯娘歌。

translations.literal: 」 There was also the Awei-niang song.
translations.idiomatic: " There was also the Awei-niang song.

sentences.zh: 時又謠曰：「可憐聖善寺，身著綠毛衣，牽來河裏飲，踏殺鯉魚兒。

translations.literal: At the time there was again a rhyme saying: "可憐聖善寺, 身著綠毛衣, 牽來河裏飲, 踏殺鯉魚兒.
translations.idiomatic: At the time another rhyme ran: "Pitiable Shengshan Temple—clad in a green wool coat, led to the river to drink, trampling the carp to death.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在潞州，有童謠曰：「羊頭山北作朝堂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong was at Luzhou, there was a children's rhyme saying: "羊頭山北作朝堂.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong was at Luzhou, a children's rhyme ran: "North of Yangtou Mountain, build the court hall.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，有術士李遐周於玄都觀院廡間為詩曰：「燕市人皆去，函關馬不歸，人逢山下鬼，環上繫羅衣。

translations.literal: During Tianbao, the adept Li Xiazhou wrote a poem in the corridor of Xuandu Temple saying: "燕市人皆去, 函關馬不歸, 人逢山下鬼, 環上繫羅衣.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era (742–756), the adept Li Xiazhou wrote a poem in the corridor of Xuandu Temple: "The people of Yan's market all depart; the horses of Hangu Pass do not return. One meets the ghost beneath the mountain; on the ring a gauze robe is tied.

sentences.zh: 」而人皆不悟，近詩妖也。

translations.literal: 」 Yet people all did not understand—near a poetic omen.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet no one understood the portent—it was a case of poetic omen.

sentences.zh: 又祿山未反時，童謠曰：「燕燕飛上天，天上女兒鋪白氈，氈上有千錢。

translations.literal: Again, before Lushan rebelled, a children's rhyme said: "燕燕飛上天, 天上女兒鋪白氈, 氈上有千錢.
translations.idiomatic: Before An Lushan rebelled, a children's rhyme ran: "Swallows fly up to heaven; a heavenly maiden spreads white felt; on the felt lie a thousand coins.

sentences.zh: 」時幽州又有謠曰：「舊來誇戴竿，今日不堪看，但看五月裏，清水河邊見契丹。

translations.literal: 」 At the time Youzhou also had a rhyme saying: "舊來誇戴竿, 今日不堪看, 但看五月裏, 清水河邊見契丹.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Youzhou also had a rhyme: "Once they boasted of Dai's pole; today it is unfit to look upon—just watch in the fifth month, and by the Qing River you will see the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 德宗時，或為詩曰：「此水連涇水，雙眸血滿川，青牛逐朱虎，方號太平年。

translations.literal: During Dezong, someone wrote a poem saying: "此水連涇水, 雙眸血滿川, 青牛逐朱虎, 方號太平年.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Dezong's reign, someone wrote a poem: "This water joins the Jing River; both eyes fill the stream with blood; a green ox chases a red tiger—and then they call it a year of great peace.

sentences.zh: 」近詩妖也。

translations.literal: 」 Near a poetic omen.
translations.idiomatic: " It was another poetic omen.

sentences.zh: 朱泚未敗前兩月，有童謠曰：「一隻筯，兩頭朱，五六月，化為胆。

translations.literal: Two months before Zhu Ci was defeated, there was a children's rhyme saying: "一隻筯, 兩頭朱, 五六月, 化為胆.
translations.idiomatic: Two months before Zhu Ci's defeat, a children's rhyme ran: "One chopstick, red at both ends—in the fifth or sixth month it turns to gall.

sentences.zh: 元和初，童謠曰：「朾麥朾麥三三三。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, a children's rhyme said: "朾麥朾麥三三三.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era (806), a children's rhyme ran: "Zheng mai, zheng mai—three, three, three.

sentences.zh: 」乃轉身曰：「舞了也。

translations.literal: 」 Then turning around it said: "舞了也.
translations.idiomatic: " Then turning around it added: "The dance is finished.

sentences.zh: 大中末，京師小兒疊布漬水，紐之向日，謂之曰「拔暈」。

translations.literal: At the end of Dazhong, capital children stacked cloth soaked in water, twisted it toward the sun, and called it "ba yun."
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Dazhong era (859), children in the capital stacked wet cloth, twisted it toward the sun, and called the game "pulling the dizzy spell."

sentences.zh: 咸通七年，童謠曰：「草青青，被嚴霜，鵲始後，看顛狂。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xiantong, a children's rhyme said: "草青青, 被嚴霜, 鵲始後, 看顛狂.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xiantong (866), a children's rhyme ran: "Grass green-green, struck by hard frost—after the magpie begins, watch for madness.

sentences.zh: 」十四年，成都童謠曰：「咸通癸巳，出無所之，蛇去馬來，道路稍開，頭無片瓦，地有殘灰。

translations.literal: 」 In the fourteenth year, a Chengdu children's rhyme said: "咸通癸巳, 出無所之, 蛇去馬來, 道路稍開, 頭無片瓦, 地有殘灰.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourteenth year (873), a Chengdu children's rhyme ran: "Xiantong, year guisi—go out with nowhere to go; the snake departs and the horse comes; the road opens a little; not a tile on the head, but ash on the ground.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，歲陰在巳，明年在午。

translations.literal: 」 That year the year-branch was in si; the next year was in wu.
translations.idiomatic: " That year the cyclical branch was si; the following year would be wu.

sentences.zh: 巳，蛇也；

translations.literal: Si is the snake;
translations.idiomatic: Si corresponds to the snake;

sentences.zh: 午，馬也。

translations.literal: wu is the horse.
translations.idiomatic: wu corresponds to the horse.

sentences.zh: 僖宗時，童謠曰：「金色蝦蟆爭努眼，翻却曹州天下反。

translations.literal: During Xizong, a children's rhyme said: "金色蝦蟆爭努眼, 翻却曹州天下反.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xizong's reign, a children's rhyme ran: "Golden toads strain their eyes—overturn Caozhou and the realm rises in revolt.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年，童謠曰：「八月無霜寒草青，將軍騎馬出空城，漢家天子西巡狩，猶向江東更索兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianfu, a children's rhyme said: "八月無霜寒草青, 將軍騎馬出空城, 漢家天子西巡狩, 猶向江東更索兵.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qianfu (879), a children's rhyme ran: "In the eighth month, no frost yet the cold grass is green; a general rides out of an empty city; the Son of Heaven of Han hunts westward—yet still seeks troops from the lands east of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 中和初，童謠曰：「黃巢走，泰山東，死在翁家翁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe, a children's rhyme said: "黃巢走, 泰山東, 死在翁家翁.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhonghe era (881), a children's rhyme ran: "Huang Chao flees east of Mount Tai—he dies at old man Weng's house, old man Weng.

sentences.zh: 訛言。

translations.literal: False rumors.
translations.idiomatic: False rumors.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十七年七月，民訛言官遣棖棖殺人，以祭天狗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, the people falsely rumored that the government sent "cheng cheng" to kill people as sacrifice to the Heavenly Dog.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventeenth year of Zhenguan (643), a rumor spread that officials had sent demon-hunters called "cheng cheng" to kill people as sacrifices to the Heavenly Dog.

sentences.zh: 云其來也，身衣狗皮，鐵爪，每於闇中取人心肝而去。

translations.literal: They said when it came, its body wore dog skin and iron claws, and each time in the dark it took people's hearts and livers and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They said the creature wore dog skin and iron claws, and in the dark it would seize people's hearts and livers and vanish.

sentences.zh: 於是更相震怖，每夜驚擾，皆引弓劍自防，無兵器者剡竹為之，郊外不敢獨行。

translations.literal: Thereupon people were mutually terrified; each night there was alarm and disturbance; all drew bows and swords to defend themselves—those without weapons carved bamboo into them—and in the suburbs no one dared walk alone.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread; every night the city was thrown into alarm. People armed themselves with bows and swords, and those without weapons carved bamboo substitutes; no one dared walk alone in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 太宗惡之，令通夜開諸坊門，宣旨慰諭，月餘乃止。

translations.literal: Taizong detested it; he ordered all ward gates kept open through the night and issued edicts of reassurance; after more than a month it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong abhorred the panic. He ordered ward gates kept open all night and sent edicts of reassurance; after more than a month the scare subsided.

sentences.zh: 武后時，民飲酒謳歌，曲終而不盡者，謂之「族鹽」。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu, when the people drank wine and sang songs, those whose tunes ended yet were not finished they called "zu yan."
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, when people drank and sang, a song whose melody ended but whose words were not exhausted was called "clan salt."

sentences.zh: 開元二十七年十月，改作東都明堂，訛言官取小兒埋明堂下，以為厭勝。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan, as the Eastern Capital Bright Hall was being rebuilt, a false rumor said officials took children and buried them beneath the Bright Hall as a victory charm.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kaiyuan 27 (739), while the Bright Hall in the Eastern Capital was being rebuilt, a rumor spread that officials were burying children beneath it as a ritual to ward off misfortune.

sentences.zh: 村野兒童藏于山谷，都城騷然，或言兵至。

translations.literal: Village and countryside children hid in mountain valleys; the capital was in uproar; some said troops had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Children in villages and the countryside hid in the hills; the capital was in uproar, and some said soldiers were coming.

sentences.zh: 玄宗惡之，遣使慰諭，久之乃止。

translations.literal: Xuanzong detested it; he sent envoys to reassure them; after a long time it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was troubled by the panic and sent envoys to reassure the people; only after a long while did the disturbance die down.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載二月辛亥，有星如月，墜于東南，墜後有聲，京師訛言官遣棖棖捕人，取肝以祭天狗，人頗恐懼，畿內尤甚，遣使安諭之，與貞觀十七年占同。

translations.literal: On xinhai in the second month of the third year of Tianbao, a star like the moon fell in the southeast; after falling there was a sound; the capital falsely rumored officials sent "cheng cheng" to seize people and take livers to sacrifice to the Heavenly Dog; people were quite fearful, especially within the capital region; envoys were sent to reassure them—the same omen as the seventeenth year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day in the second month of Tianbao 3 (744), a moon-sized star fell in the southeast with a sound afterward. The capital rumor of "cheng cheng" demon-hunters seizing livers for the Heavenly Dog spread again; fear was widespread, especially in the capital region. Envoys were dispatched to calm the people—the same portent as in Zhenguan 17.

sentences.zh: 天寶後，詩人多為憂苦流寓之思，及寄興于江湖僧寺。

translations.literal: After Tianbao, poets mostly had thoughts of sorrow, hardship, and exile, and placed their inspiration in rivers, lakes, and monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianbao era, poets increasingly wrote of sorrow, hardship, and exile, finding their themes on rivers, lakes, and in Buddhist temples.

sentences.zh: 而樂曲亦多以邊地為名，有伊州、甘州、涼州等，至其曲遍繁聲，皆謂之「入破」。

translations.literal: Moreover musical pieces also mostly took frontier regions as names—there were Yizhou, Ganzhou, Liangzhou, and so on; when the piece reached its elaborate, dense passage, all called it "ru po."
translations.idiomatic: Musical pieces too were often named for frontier regions—Yizhou, Ganzhou, Liangzhou, and the like—and when a tune reached its dense, elaborate climax, it was called "entering the break."

sentences.zh: 又有胡旋舞，本出康居，以旋轉便捷為巧，時又尚之。

translations.literal: There was also the Hu-whirl dance, originally from Kangju, taking swift rotation as its skill; at the time it was again esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Hu whirl dance, originally from Kangju, prized for its swift spinning; the age admired it.

sentences.zh: 破者，蓋破碎云。

translations.literal: "Po" (break)—it is roughly "shattering," they say.
translations.idiomatic: "Break" here meant shattering—a sign of ruin.

sentences.zh: 建中三年秋，江淮訛言有毛人食其心，人情大恐。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Jianzhong, in the Jiang-Huai region a false rumor said there were hairy men who ate people's hearts; popular sentiment was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Jianzhong 3 (782), a rumor spread through the Jiang-Huai region of hairy men who devoured human hearts, and the people were terrified.

sentences.zh: 朱泚既僭號，名其舊第曰潛龍宮，移內府珍貨以實之。

translations.literal: After Zhu Ci usurped the title, he named his old residence the Hidden Dragon Palace and moved inner-palace precious goods to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci declared himself emperor, he named his old residence the Hidden Dragon Palace and stocked it with treasures from the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 占者以為易稱「潛龍勿用」，此敗祥也。

translations.literal: Diviners thought the Changes says "the hidden dragon—do not employ it"; this was an omen of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners cited the Changes: "The hidden dragon—do not act"—and took this as an omen of defeat.

sentences.zh: 大和九年，京師訛言鄭注為上合金丹，生取小兒心肝，密旨捕小兒無算。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dahe, the capital falsely rumored that Zheng Zhu was compounding elixir pills for the emperor, taking children's hearts and livers alive; secret orders seized children beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe 9 (835), the capital rumor held that Zheng Zhu was making elixir pills for the emperor by seizing children's hearts and livers alive; secret orders were said to have taken untold numbers of children.

sentences.zh: 往往陰相告曰：「某處失幾兒矣。

translations.literal: Often people secretly told one another: "Such-and-such a place has lost several children.
translations.idiomatic: People whispered to one another: "So many children have vanished from such-and-such a place.

sentences.zh: 」方士言金丹可致神仙，蓋誕妄不經之語，或信而服之，則發熱多死，如有所戒云。

translations.literal: 」 Adepts said golden elixir could attain immortals—this was wild, absurd talk; some believed and ingested it, then fevered and mostly died, as if there were a warning.
translations.idiomatic: " Adepts claimed golden elixir could make one immortal—absurd nonsense—but those who believed and took it mostly died of fever, as if heaven itself were warning against it.

sentences.zh: 小兒，無辜者，取其心肝，將有殺戮象。

translations.literal: Children—the innocent—taking their hearts and livers: there would be an image of slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing the hearts and livers of innocent children foretold slaughter.

sentences.zh: 劉從諫未死時，潞州有狂人折腰於市曰：「石雄七千人至矣。

translations.literal: Before Liu Congjian died, in Luzhou a madman bowed at the waist in the market saying: "Shi Xiong's seven thousand men have arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before Liu Congjian died, a madman in Luzhou bowed in the market and cried: "Shi Xiong's seven thousand men have arrived.

sentences.zh: 」從諫捕斬之。

translations.literal: 」 Congjian had him seized and executed.
translations.idiomatic: " Congjian had him arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 咸通十四年秋，成都訛言有㹫母鬼夜入人家，民皆恐，夜則聚坐。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourteenth year of Xiantong, Chengdu falsely rumored there was a "tan mu" ghost entering households at night; the people were all afraid; at night they gathered to sit together.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Xiantong 14 (873), Chengdu rumor told of a "tan mu" demon entering homes at night; the people were terrified and sat together in groups after dark.

sentences.zh: 或曰某家見鬼，眼晃然如燈焰，民益懼。

translations.literal: Some said such-and-such a household saw the ghost; its eyes flickered like lamp flames; the people grew more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Some said a household had seen the ghost, its eyes flickering like lamp flames, and fear deepened.

sentences.zh: 黃巢未入京師時，都人以黃米及黑豆屑蒸食之，謂之「黃賊打黑賊」。

translations.literal: Before Huang Chao entered the capital, capital people steamed and ate yellow millet mixed with black bean crumbs, calling it "Yellow Bandit strikes Black Bandit."
translations.idiomatic: Before Huang Chao entered the capital, people steamed yellow millet mixed with black bean crumbs and called the dish "Yellow Bandit beats Black Bandit."

sentences.zh: 僖宗時，里巷鬬者激怒，言：「任見右廂天子。

translations.literal: During Xizong, brawlers in lanes and alleys, enraged, said: "Just wait till you see the Son of Heaven of the Right Wing.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xizong's reign, brawlers in the alleys, in a rage, would say: "Just wait until you see the Son of Heaven of the Right Wing.

sentences.zh: 毛蟲之孽。

translations.literal: Calamities of hairy insects.
translations.idiomatic: Calamities involving hairy beasts.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，河源軍有狼三，晝入軍門，射之，斃。

translations.literal: During Yonghui, at Heyuan Army there were three wolves; by day they entered the army gate; they were shot and killed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era (650–655), three wolves entered the gate of Heyuan Army by daylight and were shot dead.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，嵐、勝州兔害稼，千萬為羣，食苗盡，兔亦不復見。

translations.literal: During Yongchun, in Lan and Sheng prefectures rabbits harmed the crops; tens of millions formed groups, ate the seedlings clean, and the rabbits were no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchun era (682), rabbits in Lan and Sheng prefectures ravaged the crops in swarms of millions, devouring every seedling before vanishing entirely.

sentences.zh: 開元三年，有熊晝入揚州城。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan, a bear entered Yangzhou city by day.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 3 (715), a bear entered Yangzhou city in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年十月，詔百官上勤政樓觀安西兵赴陝州，有狐出于樓上，獲之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Qianyuan, an edict ordered the hundred officials to ascend Qinzheng Tower to watch Anxi troops proceed to Shanzhou; a fox emerged from atop the tower and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Qianyuan 2 (759), officials were ordered to Qinzheng Tower to watch Anxi troops march toward Shanzhou; a fox appeared on the tower and was caught.

sentences.zh: 大曆四年八月己卯，虎入京師長壽坊宰臣元載家廟，射殺之。

translations.literal: On jimao in the eighth month of the fourth year of Dali, a tiger entered Chief Minister Yuan Zai's family temple in Changshou Ward of the capital; it was shot and killed.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day in the eighth month of Dali 4 (769), a tiger entered Chief Minister Yuan Zai's family temple in Changshou Ward, Beijing, and was shot dead.

sentences.zh: 虎，西方之屬，威猛吞噬，刑戮之象。

translations.literal: The tiger belongs to the West; fierce and devouring—it is an image of punishment and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger belongs to the West—fierce and devouring—an omen of punishment and slaughter.

sentences.zh: 六年八月丁丑，獲白兔于太極殿之內廊。

translations.literal: On dingchou in the eighth month of the sixth year, a white rabbit was captured in the inner corridor of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day in the eighth month of the sixth year (771), a white rabbit was caught in the inner corridor of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「國有憂。

translations.literal: Divination says: "The state has sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Divination reads: "The state faces grief.

sentences.zh: 白，喪祥也。

translations.literal: White is an omen of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: White is an omen of mourning.

sentences.zh: 建中三年九月己亥夜，虎入宣陽里，傷人二，詰朝獲之。

translations.literal: On the night of jihai in the ninth month of the third year of Jianzhong, a tiger entered Xuanyang Lane, wounded two people; the next morning it was captured.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of jihai in the ninth month of Jianzhong 3 (782), a tiger entered Xuanyang Lane, injuring two people; it was captured the next morning.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年二月乙丑，有野鹿至于含元殿前，獲之；

translations.literal: On yichou in the second month of the second year of Zhenyuan, a wild deer came before the Hall of Encompassing Primacy and was captured;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day in the second month of Zhenyuan 2 (786), a wild deer came before the Hall of Encompassing Primacy and was captured;

sentences.zh: 壬申，又有鹿至于含元殿前，獲之。

translations.literal: On renshen, again a deer came before the Hall of Encompassing Primacy and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day, another deer came before the Hall of Encompassing Primacy and was captured.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有大喪。

translations.literal: Divination says: "There will be great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Divination reads: "Great mourning will follow.

sentences.zh: 」四年三月癸亥，有鹿至京師西市門，獲之。

translations.literal: 」 In the third month of the fourth year on guihai, a deer came to the West Market Gate of the capital and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third month of the fourth year (788), on guihai day, a deer came to the West Market Gate of the capital and was captured.

sentences.zh: 開成四年四月，有麞出于太廟，獲之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Kaicheng, a river-deer appeared in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Kaicheng 4 (839), a river-deer appeared in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was captured.

sentences.zh: 犬禍。

translations.literal: Calamities of dogs.
translations.idiomatic: Calamities involving dogs.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，突厥處羅可汗將入寇，夜聞犬羣嘷而不見犬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, when the Türk Chulo Qaghan was about to invade, at night they heard a pack of dogs howling yet saw no dogs.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3 (620), as the Türk Chulo Qaghan prepared to invade, people heard dogs howling at night but saw no dogs.

sentences.zh: 武后初，酷吏丘神勣家狗生子皆無首，當項有孔如口，晝夜鳴吠，俄失所在。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Empress Wu, the harsh official Qiu Shenji's household dogs gave birth—all without heads; at the neck was a hole like a mouth; day and night they barked; soon they vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Empress Wu's reign, the harsh official Qiu Shenji's dogs whelped headless pups with mouth-like holes in their necks; they barked day and night, then vanished.

sentences.zh: 神功元年，安國獻兩首犬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengong, Anguo presented a two-headed dog.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengong 1 (697), Anguo presented a two-headed dog.

sentences.zh: 首多者，上不一也。

translations.literal: Many heads mean the ruler is not one.
translations.idiomatic: Many heads signified that the ruler was not one.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載，李林甫晨起盥飾將朝，取書囊視之，中有物如鼠，躍于地即變為狗，壯大雄目，張牙視林甫，林甫射之，中，殺然有聲，隨箭沒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao, Li Linfu rose in the morning, washed and adorned himself to attend court; he took his book pouch and looked—inside was something like a rat; leaping to the ground it immediately changed into a dog, large and strong with great eyes; baring its teeth it stared at Linfu; Linfu shot it, hit it; there was a crack like killing; it vanished with the arrow.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 11 (752), Li Linfu was dressing for court when he opened his book pouch and found something like a rat. It leapt to the floor and became a large, fierce-eyed dog that bared its teeth at him. Linfu shot it; there was a sharp crack, and it vanished with the arrow.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年，趙州柏鄉民李崇貞家黃犬乳犢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenyuan, Li Chongzhen of Baixiang, Zhao prefecture—his yellow dog nursed a calf.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 7 (791), Li Chongzhen of Baixiang in Zhao prefecture had a yellow dog that nursed a calf.

sentences.zh: 會昌三年，定州深澤令家狗生角。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huichang, the magistrate of Shenze in Ding prefecture's household dog grew horns.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang 3 (843), a dog in the magistrate of Shenze's household in Ding prefecture grew horns.

sentences.zh: 大中初，狗生角。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong, dogs grew horns.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dazhong era (847), dogs were reported growing horns.

sentences.zh: 京房曰：「執正失將害之應。

translations.literal: Jing Fang said: "Upholding rectitude yet losing the general—this is the response of harm.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang wrote: "When rectitude is upheld yet the general is lost—this is the omen of harm.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「君子危陷，則狗生角。

translations.literal: 」 Again he said: "When gentlemen are endangered and trapped, dogs grow horns.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote: "When gentlemen fall into peril, dogs grow horns.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，會稽有狗生而不能吠，擊之無聲。

translations.literal: During Xiantong, in Kuaiji there was a dog born yet unable to bark; striking it produced no sound.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong era (860–874), in Kuaiji a dog was born unable to bark; beating it produced no sound.

sentences.zh: 狗職吠以守禦，其不能者，象鎮守者不能禦寇之兆。

translations.literal: A dog's duty is to bark to guard and defend; when it cannot, it is an omen that defenders cannot repel invaders.
translations.idiomatic: A dog's duty is to bark in defense; one that cannot bark foretold that those charged with defense would fail against invaders.

sentences.zh: 成汭為荊南節度使，城中犬皆夜吠，日者向隱以為城郭將丘墟。

translations.literal: Cheng Rui was military commissioner of Jingnan; in the city all dogs barked at night; the day-calculator Xiang Yin took it to mean the walls and moats would become ruins.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Rui was military commissioner of Jingnan, every dog in the city barked at night; the calendrist Xiang Yin interpreted this as a sign that the city would become a ruin.

sentences.zh: 中和二年秋，丹徒狗與彘交。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Zhonghe, in Dantu a dog mated with a pig.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Zhonghe 2 (882), in Dantu a dog mated with a pig.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「諸侯有謀害國者。

translations.literal: Divination says: "Among the feudal lords there are those who plot to harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: Divination reads: "Feudal lords plot to harm the state.

sentences.zh: 白眚白祥。

translations.literal: White calamities and white auspices.
translations.idiomatic: White calamities and white auspices.

sentences.zh: 調露元年十一月壬午，秦州神亭冶北霧開如日初耀，有白鹿、白狼見。

translations.literal: On renwu in the eleventh month of the first year of Tiaolu, north of Shentingye in Qin prefecture the fog opened like the sun's first radiance; a white deer and white wolf were seen.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day in the eleventh month of Tiaolu 1 (679), north of Shentingye in Qin prefecture the fog parted like the first light of dawn, and a white deer and white wolf were seen.

sentences.zh: 近白祥也。

translations.literal: Near a white auspice.
translations.idiomatic: It was a case of white auspice.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年四月己亥，雨毛于越州之鄮縣。

translations.literal: On jihai in the fourth month of the second year of Shenlong, hair rained in Mao county of Yue prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the fourth month of Shenlong 2 (706), hair rained down in Mao county, Yue prefecture.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「邪人進，賢人遁。

translations.literal: Divination says: "Evil men advance; worthy men withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Divination reads: "Evil men advance and worthy men withdraw.

sentences.zh: 大曆二年七月甲戌日入時，有白氣亙天。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Dali, on jiaxu at sunset, there was white vapor spanning heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day at sunset in the seventh month of Dali 2 (767), white vapor stretched across the sky.

sentences.zh: 九月戊午夜，白霧起西北，亙天。

translations.literal: On the night of wuwu in the ninth month, white mist rose in the northwest, spanning heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of wuwu in the ninth month, white mist rose from the northwest and filled the sky.

sentences.zh: 五年五月甲申，西北有白氣亙天。

translations.literal: On jiashen in the fifth month of the fifth year, in the northwest there was white vapor spanning heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day in the fifth month of the fifth year (770), white vapor in the northwest spanned the heavens.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十年九月庚辰甲夜，有白氣八，東西際天。

translations.literal: On gengchen in the ninth month of the twentieth year of Zhenyuan, on the night of jia, there were eight white vapors, east and west reaching heaven's edge.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day in the ninth month of Zhenyuan 20 (804), on jia night eight white vapors stretched from east to west across the sky.

sentences.zh: 大和三年八月，西方有白氣如柱。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Dahe, in the west there was white vapor like a pillar.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Dahe 3 (829), a pillar-like white vapor appeared in the west.

sentences.zh: 七年十月已酉，西方又有白氣如柱者三。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year on jiyou, in the west again there were three white vapors like pillars.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day in the tenth month of the seventh year (833), three pillar-like white vapors again appeared in the west.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年四月，有白氣頭黑如髮，自東南入于揚州滅。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Guangqi, there was white vapor with a black head like hair; from the southeast it entered Yangzhou and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Guangqi 2 (886), a white vapor with a black, hair-like head entered Yangzhou from the southeast and disappeared.

sentences.zh: 光化二年三月乙巳，日中有白氣亙天，自西南貫于東北。

translations.literal: On yisi in the third month of the second year of Guanghua, within the sun there was white vapor spanning heaven, from southwest piercing through to northeast.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day in the third month of Guanghua 2 (899), white vapor within the sun spanned the heavens from southwest to northeast.

sentences.zh: 天復元年八月己亥，西方有白雲如履底，中出白氣如匹練，長五丈，上衝天，分為三彗，頭下垂。

translations.literal: On jihai in the eighth month of the first year of Tianfu, in the west there was white cloud like a sole of a shoe; from within emerged white vapor like a bolt of silk, five zhang long, rushing upward to heaven, dividing into three comets with heads hanging down.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the eighth month of Tianfu 1 (901), in the west a white cloud shaped like a shoe sole appeared; from it white vapor like a bolt of silk, five zhang long, shot upward and split into three comet-like tails hanging down.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天下有兵。

translations.literal: Divination says: "Under Heaven there will be war.
translations.idiomatic: Divination reads: "War will spread across the realm.

sentences.zh: 白者，戰祥也。

translations.literal: White is an omen of battle.
translations.idiomatic: White is an omen of battle.

sentences.zh: 木沴金。

translations.literal: Wood harms metal.
translations.idiomatic: Subsection: wood overcoming metal.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，東都白馬寺鐵像頭無故自落於殿門外。

translations.literal: During Shenlong, at the Eastern Capital's White Horse Temple the iron statue's head for no reason fell off by itself outside the hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era (705–707), at White Horse Temple in the Eastern Capital the head of an iron statue fell off by itself outside the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 天寶五載四月，宰臣李適之常列鼎具膳羞，中夜，鼎躍出相鬬不解，鼎耳及足皆折。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Tianbao, Chief Minister Li Shizhi often set out tripods with prepared delicacies; in the middle of the night the tripods leapt out and fought one another without ceasing; the tripod ears and legs all broke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tianbao 5 (746), Chief Minister Li Shizhi had set out tripods with a feast when at midnight the tripods leapt up and fought one another; their ears and legs all snapped off.
